Preflight names no collision check for an existing client-owned file at an archive destination. Preflight names no collision check for an existing client-owned file at an archive destination. The proposed git show <old>:<path> restore hint cannot work for a client file that Forge never shipped at <old>. That is one of the named refusal cases and needs different actionable advice (CORE.md:134-139).

The rollback's git clean -fd cannot remove a newly created file ignored by the client's rules. For example, ensure_missing can create a missing .envrc, while the preflight only looks for ignored files already at write destinations; an ignored new file survives both git add -A and rollback (CORE.md:137-138,158-160,171-174; factory/scripts/forge_cli/upgrade.py:4817-4825).

The rollback guard explicitly covers Exception and SystemExit but not KeyboardInterrupt or termination after branch creation. An interrupted upgrade can therefore leave the branch and changed client state despite the exact-rollback promise (CORE.md:65-66,171-174; docs/specs/simple-upgrade.md:82-85).

The plan permits a detached target by recording its SHA for rollback, yet tells the user to open a PR into that original SHA. A SHA is not a usable PR base branch; detached targets need a refusal or a defined branch destination (CORE.md:142-144,175-178).

The approved story plan puts OLD-CLIENT-FIXTURE before CORE and makes CORE depend on it; the recorded decomposition removes that task, folds its deliverable into dependency-free CORE, and collapses the remaining six-task graph to three. The plan promises refusals leave git-local Forge state unchanged, while the existing exclusion lock creates or truncates a file under <git-dir>/forge/locks and leaves it after release.
